ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md` (the skill requires this before every fix round).
ACTION: Read `fetch/retry.py` around line 41 to check whether `attempt` starts at 0 or 1, so I know the reviewer's off-by-one reading is right.
ACTION: Run a throwaway script, kept outside the repo, that calls the retry wrapper with a stub that always times out and counts the calls. This reproduces the extra retry before I edit.
ACTION: Edit `fetch/retry.py:41`, changing `attempt > max_retries` to `attempt >= max_retries`, only if the check confirms F1.
ACTION: Re-run the throwaway count check and `tests/test_retry.py`, and read the output.
ACTION: Commit the fix.
ACTION: Append a note to the implementer's report file in `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/`. It says I made the fix myself on your instruction, that it changes behavior, and that no test pins the retry count.
ACTION: Run `scripts/review-package` on the plan file and the fix commit range, and note the diff path it reports.
ACTION: Dispatch a scoped re-review on `sonnet` using `re-review-prompt.md`, with that diff path. Its purpose is a verdict of ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED on F1, and a check for new Critical or Important findings.

Message to partner:

I am fixing F1 myself, as you asked. The skill normally sends a behavior change to a fix subagent, even a one-character change, and `>` to `>=` changes what the code does. Your instruction names this case, so I follow it.

First I will check that the reviewer read the code correctly. If `attempt` starts at 1, F1 is wrong and I will say so instead of editing. If it is right, I will make the edit, run `tests/test_retry.py` and send the fix to a scoped re-review.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `tests/test_retry.py` checks that a retry happens, not how many. The off-by-one passes that test, and the fix will pass it too.
- To check the fix, I will count calls with a throwaway stub. A test that asserts the exact call count would protect it for good. I will add one only if you want it.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
